description_en: The Gokarṇeśvara Temple is a sacred pilgrimage site of great religious and historical significance in Nepal. Gokarṇeśvara Mahādeva is considered to have immense sanctity, second only to Paśupati. The Hindus and Buddhists of Nepal hold it with equal importance and reverence. Hindus worship the deity in this temple as a form of Mahādeva (Śiva), while Buddhists worship it as Gaganagaṃja Bodhisattva. Similarly, Hindus regard this tīrtha as one of the sixty-four Śivaliṅgas, while Buddhists have traditionally revered it as the foremost and most ancient among the theAṣṭavaitarāgapilgrimage site.The origin of Gokarṇeśvara is described by an interesting mythological tale in theBhāṣāvaṃśāvalī. In theSatyayuga(Golden Age), when Mahādeva, took the form of a deer and was wandering in theŚleṣamāntakaforest, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Indra saw him and tried to capture him. As all three of them grabbed hold of an antler, it broke into three pieces and fell into their hands. The piece that fell into Viṣṇu's hand was taken toAmarāvatī(Indra's celestial city) for installation, the piece that fell into Indra's hand was taken toPātālaloka(the netherworld) for installation, while the piece that fell into Brahmā's hand was installed on the banks of the Bāgmatī River near the Gokarṇa Pihāmaha Tīrtha, thus establishing Gokarṇeśvara (N. Pouḍela, VS 2020, p. 16). The Gokarṇeśvara Temple is situated on the banks of the Bāgmatī in Gokarṇa. The three ancient temples of Nepal located on the banks of the Bāgmatī are Paśupati, Jalavināyaka, and Gokarṇeśvara. Built in the Nepalese tiered style, this temple has three roofs. On the very top of the temple, a golden pinnacle and an umbrella (chatra) have been installed. Next to the pinnacle, a trident has also been placed, while the four corners of each of the three roofs are covered with brass. On the ground floor, a sanctum sanctorum has been constructed. A Śivaliṅga made of stone is installed at the center. The temple, built facing east, has doors on all four sides. The main entrance on the east is covered with copper plates. Atoraṇais fixed above the door. At the center of the torana, figures of Mahādeva and Pārvatī are carved, and the torana is also covered with copper plates. The struts here are carved with various gods and goddesses, which adds to the temple's artistry and beauty. In front of the western door, a Nandi is installed. To the south of the temple, there is a large bell. This bell was offered by the younger Queen Lalitatripurāsundarī of Raṇabahādura Śāha in 1825 CE (VS 1885). All around the temple, one can see numerous idols of various gods and goddesses installed. The main door covered with gold-gilded copper, and many of the idols here were established by Balabhañjana Pāṇḍe. In the north-western corner of the temple, there is a temple of Pārvatī. The idol of Pārvatī installed in the temple's sanctum is considered the power of Gokarṇeśvara Mahādeva, and the craftsmanship of this idol is considered very beautiful.Although there is evidence that King Jayasthiti  Malla  first restored the temple and brought it to its current form, no facts have been obtained regarding who built the initial temple and when. In 1392 CE (NS 512), King Jayasthiti Malla restored this temple, appointed a Southern Bhaṭṭa priest to perform worship, and also established a religious endowment. From that time until now, worship has been continuously performed here through the Southern Bhaṭṭa Brahmaṇa (Ś. Śreṣṭha, VS 2045, p. 24). Inscriptions are affixed to the wall at the northern corner of the temple. Among these inscriptions, the one from 1583 CE (ŚS 777) from the reign of Śivasiṃhadeva and Raṇajītasiṃha is the oldest, which mentions that Gopirāma Bhāro installed a golden pinnacle on the temple. Looking at past history, it appears that the temple's restoration occurred at various times. According to details mentioned in an inscription dated 1693 CE (NS 813) located on a pāṭī within the Gokarṇeśvara courtyard, 3 ropaṇīs of land were allocated for the restoration of the śivālaya and for applying lime annually (S. Bhaṇḍārī, VS 2068, p. 32). In 1787 CE (NS 908), Dharmanārāyaṇa constructed a pāṭī and a dharmaśālā on the southern side of the temple for the salvation of ancestors (pitṛ uddāra) and established an endowment (GKN0010_I_002). In the past, only the topmost roof of the temple was covered with brass, while the other roofs had brick tiles. That top roof was restored, and during the reign of Raṇabahādur Śāha, in 1830 CE (SS 1759), a brass roof with gold gilding was installed. Similarly, the main entrance on the east was covered with gold-gilded copper plates by Balabhañjana Pāṇḍe in 1846 CE (VS 1902). This shows that people from different periods have carried out restoration work on the temple, giving it great importance. More recently, in 2023 CE (VS 2080), the temple's roofs were reconstructed and all three roofs were covered with gold-gilded copper plates.Jayasthiti Malla, in 1392 CE (NS 512), appointed a Southern Bhaṭṭa priest to conduct worship at this temple and established an endowment to manage the temple's annual rites. Continuing this established tradition, Southern Bhaṭṭas remain the main priests, performing all daily and religious rituals here. The change of priests follows a hereditary system. Worship and rituals are performed here according to both Vedic and Tantric methods. Every morning, the priest performs the daily worship of the Śivaliṅga by bathing it withpañcāmṛta. On festivals such asKuśe Aũsī(Father's Day),Kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī, all Mondays in the month ofŚrāvaṇa,Pauṣa Aũsī, andŚivarātrī, a large crowd of devotees gathers here. Especially on the day ofBhādrakṛṣṇa Aũsī(Father's Day), a special fair is held in this area. This festival, also known as 'Bubā ko mukha herne din' (Father’s Day) andKuśe Aũsī, has the tradition of people coming from various parts of the country to bathe in the Bāgmatī and performśrāddhaandtarpaṇain the name of their fathers and ancestors. There is a popular belief that performingPitṛśrāddha(ancestral rites) on this day yields great merit. Similarly, on the day ofMahāśivarātrī, which is observed on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Phālguna, a special fair is held here. On Mahāśivarātrī, worship is performed at this temple withṢoḍśopacāra(sixteen offerings) rites throughout all four prahara pūjā. In the fourth prahara of the night, an offering of rice pudding is made. The tradition is to perform this rice pudding offering in a very secretive manner, without even keeping an assistant priest (B. Bā̃skoṭā, VS 2063, p. 71). For special festivals, the endowment organization makes separate arrangements here.
description_ne: गोकर्णेश्वर मन्दिर नेपालको धार्मिक र ऐतिहासिक महत्त्व बोकेको पवित्र तीर्थस्थल हो । गोकर्णेश्वर महादेवलाई पशुपति पछि ठूलो महिमा भएको मानिन्छ । नेपालमा रहेको हिन्दू र बौद्धहरूले समान महत्व र श्रद्धा राख्ने गर्दछन् ।  हिन्दूहरू यस मन्दिरमा रहेको मूर्तिलाई महादेवको रूपमा र बौद्धहरू गगनगंज बोधिसत्वको रूपमा पूजा गर्दछन् । त्यसैगरी यस तीर्थस्थललाई हिन्दूहरूले ६४ शिवलिङ्गहरू मध्ये एक मानेका छन् भने बौद्धहरूले यसलाई अष्टवैतराग मध्ये सबैभन्दा जेठो तीर्थको रूममा मन्दै आएका छन् ।गोकर्णेश्वरको उत्पत्ति बारे भाषावंशावलीमा रोचक पौराणिक कथा उल्लेख गरिएको छ । सत्ययुगमा महादेव मृगरूप धारण गरी श्लेषमान्तक वन घुम्दै गरेको समयमा ब्रह्मा, विष्णु र इन्द्रले देखेर समात्न खोजे छन् । तीनै जनाले सिङमा समात्दा सिङ तीन टुक्रा भई तीनजनाको हातमा आएछन् । विष्णुको हातमा परेको सिङ अमरावतीमा स्थापना गर्न गए, इन्द्रको सातमा परेको सिङ पाताललोकमा स्थापना गर्न गए भने ब्रह्माको हातमा परेको सिङ गोकर्ण पिहामह तीर्थका समिपमा वागमतीको किनारामा स्थापना गरी गोकर्णेश्वर स्थापना भएको थियो (N. Pouḍela VS 2020, p. 16) । गोकर्णेश्वर मन्दिर गोकर्णको वागमती किनारामा अवस्थित छ । वागमती किनारामा अवस्थित नेपालका तीन प्राचीन मन्दिरहरू पशुपति,जलविनायक र गोकर्णेश्वर मन्दिर रहेको छ । नेपाली तले शैलीमा बनेको यस मन्दिर तीन तलाको रहेको छ । मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो छानामाथि सुनको गजूर र छत्र चढाइएको छ । गजूरको छेउमा त्रिशूल पनि राखिएको छ भने छानाको चारै कुनामा  मन्दिरको तीनवटै छानाहरू पितलले छाएका छन् । भुइँतलामा गर्भगृह बनाइएको छ । केन्द्रमा ढुङ्गाको शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ । पूर्वाभिमुख गरी निर्माण गरेको मन्दिरको चारैतिर ढोका बनेका छन् । पूर्वपट्टि रहेको मुख्य प्रबेशद्वारमा तामाको पाताले मोडेको छ । ढोकामाथि तोरण जडान गरिएको छ । तोरणको केन्द्रमा महादेव पार्वतीको आकृति कुदिएको छ भने तोरणलाई पनि तामाको पाताले मोडिएको छ । यहाँ रहेको टुँडालहरूमा बिभिन्न देवीदेवताहरू कुदिएको छ जसले मन्दिरलाई थप कलात्मक र सुन्दर देखाएको छ । मन्दिरको पश्चिम ढोका अघि नन्दी स्थापना गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको दक्षिणमा एउटा ठूलो घण्ट रहेको छ । उक्त घण्ट रणबहादुर शाहकी कान्छी महारानी ललितत्रिपुरासुन्दरीले विसं १८८५ (सन् १८२५) मा चढाएको थियो । मन्दिर वरपर अनेकौं देवीदेवताहरूको मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका देख्न सकिन्छ । मुख्य ढोकामा मोडिएको सुनको जलप युक्त तामा र यहाँ रहेका धेरैजसको मूर्तिहरू बलभञ्जन पाण्डेले स्थापना गरेका हुन् । मन्दिरको पश्चिमकोत्तर कोणमा पार्वतीको मन्दिर रहेको छ । मन्दिरको गर्वगृहमा स्थापित पार्वतीको मूर्ति गोकर्णेश्वर महादेवको शक्तिको रूपमा रहेको छ भने उक्त मूर्तिको बनावट निकै सुन्दर मानिन्छ ।राजा जयस्थिति मल्लले मन्दिरको पहिलो पटक जीर्णोद्धार गरी वर्तमान स्वरूपमा ल्याएको प्रमाण प्राप्त भएता पनि मन्दिरको प्रारम्भिक निर्माण कसले र कहिले निर्माण गर्यो भन्ने तथ्य प्राप्त भएको छैन । नेसं ५१२ (ई.सं. १३९२) मा राजा जयस्थिति मल्लले यस मन्दिर जीर्णोद्धार गरी दक्षिण भट्ट राखी पूजा गराएका थिए र गुठी पनि स्थापना गरेका थिए। त्यसबेलादेखि अहिलेसम्म दक्षिण भट्ट ब्राह्मणमार्फत यहाँ पूजा हुँदै आएको छ (Ś. Śreṣṭha VS 2045, p. 24) । मन्दिरको उत्तरपट्टिको कुनाको पर्खालमा यहाँ रहेको अभिलेखहरू टाँसिएका छन् । उक्त अभिलेखहरू मध्ये शिवसिंहदेव र रणजितसिंहको शासनकालमको शसं ७७७ (सन् १५८३) को अभिलेख सबैभन्दा पुरानो रहेको छ जसमा गोपिराम भारोले मन्दिरमा सुनको गजूर स्थापना गरको कुरा उल्लेख भएको छ । विगतका इतिहास हेर्दा मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार विभिन्न समयमा भएको देखिन्छ । गोकर्णश्वरको चौघराभित्र पाटीमा रहेको नेसं ८१३ (सन् १६९३) को अभिलेखमा उल्लेख विवरण अनुसार शिवालयको जीर्णोद्धारका लागि तथा प्रतिवर्ष चुना लगाउनका लागि ३ रोपनी खेत राखेको थियो (S. Bhaṇḍārī VS 2068, p. 32)। नेसं ९०८ (सन् १७८७) मा धर्मनारायणले पितृ उद्धारका लागि मन्दिरको दक्षिणपट्टिको पाटी र धर्मशाला निर्माण गरी गुठी स्थापना गरेका थिए (GKN0010_I_002) । विगतमा मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो छाना मात्र पित्तलले छाएको थियो भने अन्य छानाहरूमा झिंगटीको थियो । उक्त माथिल्लो छानालाई जीर्णोद्धार गरी शसं १७५१ (सन् १८३०) रणबहादुर शाहको शासनकालमा सुनको मोलम्वा लगाएको पित्तलको छाना राखिएको थियो । त्यसैगरी मन्दिरको पूर्वपट्टि रहेको मुख्य प्रवेशद्वारलाई विसं १९०२ (सन् १८४६) वलभञ्जन पाण्डेले सुनको मोलम्वा लगाएको तामाको पाटाले मोड्न लगाएको थियो । यसबाट विभिन्न कालखण्डमा विभिन्न मानिसहरूले महत्व दिएर मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार कार्य गर्दै आएको थाहा हुन्छ । पछिल्लो समय विसं २०८० (सन् २०२३) मा मन्दिरको छानाको पुनर्निर्माण गरी तीनवटै छानालाई सुनको मोलम्वा लगाएको तामाको पाताले मोडिएको थियो ।जयस्थिति मल्लले नेसं ५१२ (सन् १३९२) मा यस मन्दिरमा दक्षिण भट्ट राखी पूजा गराएको र मन्दिरको बार्षिक संस्कार चलाउन गुठी पनि स्थापना गरेका थिए । त्यसैलाई निरन्तरता दिँदै यहाँको मुख्य पुजारी दक्षिणको भट्टहरू रहने व्यवस्था रहेको छ र उनीहरूबाट यहाँ हुने सम्पूर्ण नित्य तथा धार्मिक कार्यहरू हुदै आइरहेको छ । पुजारी परिवर्तन वंशपरम्परामा आधारमा हुने प्रचलन रहेको छ । यहाँ वैदिक एवम् तान्त्रिक विधि अनुसार पूजा आरधना गरिन्छ । हरेक दिन विहान पुजारीले शिवलिङ्गलाई पञ्चामृत स्थान गरी नित्यपूजा गरिन्छ । कुशे औँसी, कृष्णजन्माष्टमी, साउन महिनाको सबै सोमबार, पौषे औँसी, शिवरारात्री आदि पर्वहरूमा यहाँ भक्तजनहरूको निकै भीड हुने गर्दछ । विषेशगरी भाद्रकृष्ण औँसीका दिन यस क्षत्रेमा विशेष मेला लाग्ने गर्दछ । ‘बुबाको मुख हेर्ने दिन’ र कुशे औँसी पनि भनेर मनाइने यस पर्वमा देशको विभिन्न स्थानबाट यहाँ आई वागमतीमा स्नान गर्ने र आफ्ना पिता एवम् पूर्वजहरूको नाममा श्राद्ध - तर्पण दिन चलन रहेको छ । यस दिन यहाँ पितृश्राद्ध गरेमा ठूलो पुण्य प्राप्त हुन्छ भन्ने जनविश्वार रहेको पाइन्छ । त्यसैगरी फागुण कृष्ण चतुर्दशी दिन मनाइने महाशिवरात्रीका दिन पनि यहाँ विशेष मेला लाग्ने गर्दछ । महाशिवरात्रीका दिन यस मन्दिरमा षोड्शोपचार विधिले चारै प्रहर पूजा गर्ने गरिन्छ । रात्रीको चौथौ प्रहरमा खीर भोग लगाइन्छ । खीर भोग दिने बेला सहायक पुजारीलाई पनि नराखी निकै गोप्य तरिकाले गर्ने चलन रहेको छ (B. Bā̃skoṭā, VS 2063, p. 71) । विशेष पर्वहरूको लागि गुठी सस्थानले यहाँ छुट्टै व्यवस्था मिलाउने गर्दछ ।

historical_events.event_description: King Jayasthiti Malla restored this temple, appointed a Southern Bhaṭṭa to conduct worship, and established an endowment. From that time until now, the worship has been continually performed by the Southern Bhaṭṭa Brāhmaṇas.
During the reign of Śivasiṃhadeva and Raṇajitasiṃha, an individual named Gopirāma Bhāro offered a golden pinnacle to this temple.
Threeropanīsof land were set aside for the restoration of the śivālaya and for applying lime annually.

During the reign of Raṇabahādura Śāha, Dharmanārāyaṇa, with the desire to facilitate the salvation of ancestors, constructed a rest house on the south side of Gokarna on the new moon day of Śrāvaṇa and established a land endowment for the performance of śrāddha.
A phalcā containing six bays was constructed to the east of Gokarṇeśvara Mahādeva and to the west of Cyāsiṃkhya: Bhairava.

Numerous inscriptions are affixed to the wall at the north-eastern corner of the temple. Among these, one inscription is dated 1804 CE (SS 1725). On the upper part of the inscription, figures of the Trident, the Moon, and the Sun can be seen, while the lower part features the carved image of a donor couple. As the inscription has faded, the details contained within it are not clear.
The bell located on the southern platform of the temple was offered to Gokarṇeśvara Mahādeva by Lalitatripurāsundarī, the younger Queen of Raṇabahādura Śāha.

The topmost roof of the temple consists of gold-gilded brass plates and a cast metal pinnacle. This roof was installed during the reign of Raṇabahādura Śāha in 1830 CE (SS 1751). This detail is found in the inscription located on the roof.

The eastern entrance door of this temple was constructed with gold-gilded copper plates by Balabhañjana Pāṇḍe, together with his wives Viṣṇu Kumārī and Umā Devī, his daughter Khaḍga Kumārī, and the entire family.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of Hem Nārāyaṇa and endowment of land
historical_events.event_description: Hemakarna Thapa Godar established agricultural land endowments in various locations for Hemnārāyaṇa, located east of Gokarṇeśvara Mahādeva on the banks of the Bāgmatī, and for Hema Bhakteśvara Mahādeva, located in the northeast direction.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of Śivaliṅga and endowment of land
historical_events.event_description: Mahemanisiṃha Bhaṇḍārī, along with his wife Bālakumārī, his sons Navabahādura and Sthiti Bahādura, and three daughters, established Śrī Śiva Meheravāla Bhakteśvara near this temple on the banks of the Bāgmatī. They established agricultural land endowments in various places, and arrangements were made so that the income from that land would cover the expenses for the entire year's activities.
Kaviprasād Gautama came here on the new moon day of Bhādra (Father's Day), performed śrāddha, engaged in bhajana-kīrtana (devotional singing), and additionally arranged a feast for 108 priests.

The roofs were reconstructed, and gold-gilded brass roofs were installed on all the temple's roofs. Furthermore, the Savaṅgīṇa Vikāsa Samanvaya Samiti successfully concluded the Śrīmad Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa Historical Religious Grand Fair.

This inscription is also located on the wall at the north-eastern corner of the temple. Due to the lack of clarity in the letters, it is difficult to fully comprehend the inscription's details. The date mentioned on it is also erased and cannot be ascertained. Upon a careful reading of the inscription, it can be understood that there are mentions of offering pañcāmṛta to Mahādeva on the new moon day of Śrāvaṇa, that Kāśīrāma established endowments in various locations in the temple's name, and that various worship methods are described.
As the inscription is heavily faded and many of the letters have become illegible, the details mentioned in the inscription are not in a readable condition.
